name: weasyprint-uv-run-invocation
prompt: Convert README.md in this repo to a PDF using the markdown-to-pdf skill's own conversion script.

assertions.description: Invokes the script via 'uv run --with markdown --with weasyprint python3 convert.py', not a bare pip install + python3 call
Names the bundled conversion script

name: css-override-branding
prompt: I want the PDF output to use our company's branded stylesheet instead of the default neutral one. How?

assertions.description: Uses the --css flag to override the default neutral stylesheet
Explains the bundled stylesheet is intentionally neutral and meant to be overridden

name: glob-multiple-files-output-dir
prompt: Convert all markdown files in the docs/ folder to PDFs at once, placing the results in a build/ directory.

assertions.description: Uses a glob pattern to target all markdown files, rather than listing each file individually
Uses the -o/--output-dir flag to redirect output

name: missing-css-no-silent-fallback
prompt: I passed --css branding.css but that file doesn't exist. Should the conversion silently fall back to the default style, or something else?

assertions.description: The script surfaces the missing --css path as an error rather than silently falling back to the default
Frames the missing file as an error condition

name: conversion-confirms-file-exists-nonzero
prompt: After converting report.md to PDF, how should you confirm to the user that it actually worked, not just that the command was run?

assertions.description: Names the produced .pdf file explicitly
Reports the output file size as evidence the PDF actually contains content, not just that the command exited 0

name: no-external-font-fetch
prompt: Will the PDFs generated by this skill need internet access to render fonts correctly?

assertions.description: The default stylesheet uses system fonts, so no external font fetch is needed
Names system fonts as the reason no network access is required

name: companion-branding-skill
prompt: We're producing an internal Netresearch report as a PDF — should we use the default styling, or is there something more appropriate?

assertions.description: Knows about the companion netresearch-branding-skill, which ships a matching brand stylesheet
Applies the brand stylesheet via the --css flag

name: multiple-files-per-file-report
prompt: Convert three markdown files (intro.md, chapter1.md, chapter2.md) to separate PDFs and tell me the result for each one.

assertions.description: Passes all three input files to a single conversion call rather than three separate script invocations
Reports a per-file result, matching the script's per-file output format

name: output-dir-auto-created
prompt: Convert notes.md to PDF and put the result in a dist/ folder that doesn't exist yet.

assertions.description: Uses the -o/--output-dir flag pointing at the not-yet-existing directory
Notes that the output directory gets created automatically, rather than requiring the user to mkdir first

name: no-md-files-found-asks-user
prompt: I ran the markdown-to-pdf conversion in a directory with no .md files and didn't specify which files to convert. What should happen?

assertions.description: Lists the directory contents rather than failing with a bare error
Asks the user which files to convert instead of guessing

name: weasyprint-missing-uv-auto-resolve
prompt: The conversion script reports that WeasyPrint isn't installed. What's the fix, given the skill runs via uv?

assertions.value: uv run[^\n]*--with weasyprint|uv pip install weasyprint
assertions.description: uv's --with flags should auto-resolve WeasyPrint; the fallback is 'uv pip install', not a bare 'pip install'
Keeps uv as the tool of record instead of switching to a plain pip/venv workflow

name: markdown-extensions-tables-fenced-code
prompt: My markdown source has fenced code blocks and a table. Will they render correctly in the generated PDF?

assertions.description: Knows the underlying markdown library is configured with the tables and fenced_code extensions
Confirms both constructs are supported rather than hedging

name: skill-dir-relative-css-resolution
prompt: We installed this skill at a non-standard path. Will the default stylesheet still be found when we run the conversion script?

assertions.description: The script resolves assets/style.css relative to its own file location (SKILL_DIR), so it works regardless of install path
States explicitly that the resolution is install-path independent

name: output-suffix-swap-not-append
prompt: If I convert design-spec.md without an output directory, what will the resulting PDF be named and where will it land?

assertions.description: The .md suffix is swapped for .pdf, not appended (design-spec.md -> design-spec.pdf, not design-spec.md.pdf)
Without -o, the PDF lands next to the source file rather than in a fixed default output directory

name: a4-page-size-footer-numbers
prompt: Does the default PDF styling include page numbers, and what page size does it use?

assertions.description: The bundled stylesheet targets A4 page size
The bundled stylesheet adds page numbers in the footer
